oracle.wholeBattleContextReason: Reflect the real VM global object with ordinary Script var/function binding descriptors; contextified sandbox wrappers change configurability and hide uninitialized bindings from parent reflection.
oracle.reason: Default JIT tiers and --no-opt produced different NaN bits for identical source and inputs. --jitless was stable across all six cold/warmed probe processes.
oracle.throughputPolicy: Performance measurements may use compiled native candidates or separately identified runtime flags. Qualification compares candidate traces against this pinned source profile; measurements alone do not establish equivalence.
oracle.scope: Reproducible reference implementation profile, not a claim that ECMAScript specifies NaN sign/payload or that all engine versions produce identical bits.

scope: Isolated Rust immutable parse IR plus guarded source-realm fresh materialization. Original public parser function stays untouched; this adapter is not a deployed function replacement.
proof: IR contains only input token indices and exactly representable <=9-digit nonnegative integer values; no JS heap result is cached.
Each admitted call allocates fresh ordinary result/mode/range objects in original insertion order. Repeated modes share the correct per-call mode array only.

Source parser intrinsics, dense own primitive-string inputs and absence of mode keys on the intrinsic Object prototype are checked getter-free before admission. Proxy detection uses Node host capability here; a native VM adapter must use VM object kinds.

Unsupported arrays, strings, getters, proxies, prototype collisions, coercions and changed intrinsics execute the complete original source; warnings, exceptions, input mutations, read order, exact result descriptors, aliases and f64 bits are compared.
Return values are mutated between repeated admitted calls to test cache isolation. Original public parser identity and Function.toString are retained by leaving it untouched.
limitations: No C++/Rust canonical VM adapter or original generated-C body trampoline is implemented or enabled. Native lowering must preserve original function object/metadata and check every listed intrinsic/prototype guard.
These are parser cases, not battle cases. Full callback/state trace and raw table counter equality remain required for battle deployment.
No allocation-count equivalence is claimed for GC/heap telemetry; ordinary source Cocos ClassMgr counters are not called by either original parser or IR materialization.
The old opt-in helper-level specialization remains separate and is not enabled by this proof. No throughput or speedup is measured.
